extracted.intended_audience: writers (poets and prose authors), translators, and nonprofit literary organizations interested in Lannan Foundation support
extracted.subtask_description: Description of the Lannan Foundation Literary Program's purposes, the kinds of work and organizations it supports (awards, fellowships, grants for nonprofits), historical note on translation support, and its submission policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for exceptional poetry and prose written originally in English
rubrics_metrics.description: Lannan Foundation established its Literary Program in 1987 to support the creation of exceptional poetry and prose written originally in the English language, and to increase the audience for contemporary literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Priority is on original English-language poetry and prose that contributes to contemporary literature; the program's purpose includes both creation and audience-building. (Implicit evaluative focus: literary excellence and impact on contemporary readership.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant support for works translated into English (2001–2024)
rubrics_metrics.description: Between 2001-2024, we also offered grant support for the publication and dissemination of works translated into English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This describes a historical programmatic activity (translation support) rather than a current intake policy; applicants should note the dated range when considering eligibility or past program emphases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awards and fellowships honor/promote writers whose work reflects and challenges our understanding of the world
rubrics_metrics.description: Through its annual awards and fellowships program, the foundation honored and promoted writers and poets whose work reflects and challenges our understanding of the world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluative emphasis is on work that both reflects the human/ social condition and challenges prevailing understandings — i.e., literary work with critical, reflective, or provocative dimensions. Awards/fellowships are aimed at recognition and promotion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grants to nonprofit organizations that create, promote, and widen appreciation of literature
rubrics_metrics.description: The Literary Program also made grants to nonprofit organizations engaged in creating, promoting, and widening the appreciation of literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligible organizational activity emphasizes creation, promotion, and audience development for literature. The page lists example grantees (e.g., Cave Canem, Copper Canyon Press, Graywolf Press, Words Without Borders) as models of supported nonprofit activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Production and dissemination of public literary events (Readings & Conversations)
rubrics_metrics.description: The foundation has also produced numerous public literary events, the Readings & Conversations series, which features poets and writers reading and discussing their work. You can watch and listen to these events in our media archive here.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program values public-facing literary programming and maintains a media archive for recordings of events — indicating emphasis on both live presentation and long-term dissemination/archival access.

rubrics_metrics.name: No unsolicited proposals or letters of inquiry accepted
rubrics_metrics.description: Lannan does not accept letters of inquiry in any of our grant-making programs. Unsolicited proposals and letters of inquiry will not be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a strict submission policy/procedural requirement: potential applicants should not send unsolicited materials; grants are by invitation or through established program channels only.
